brief: JPMorgan's Lakos-Bujas, who flagged extreme momentum crowding in May, now says capitulation in the momentum factor is "far along" and reverses his caution, keeping an S&P 500 target of 8,000 (8% above Friday's 7,377 close). October's long/short momentum factor fell 16% (long down 12%, short up 5%), the worst month since 1985 for the long leg; a post-midterm Thursday selloff added a 7.9-sigma momentum underperformance day. JPM lists capitulation evidence: crowding fell from the 100th to 76th percentile, levered ETFs sold roughly $60bn and now sit below January exposure, CTAs are already short, vol-targeting funds cut leverage, and QQQ's RSI dropped below 30 (historically followed by a roughly 4% five-day bounce). Missing pieces: vol-control funds still have about $50bn to sell, dealer gamma is low (two-way risk), retail stayed hesitant, and corporate buybacks shifted to capex. Separately, AI supply-chain forward P/E multiples compressed sharply (memory 8.0x to 3.2x) while earnings estimates stayed flat, meaning either valuations are cheap or earnings forecasts must fall. Hyperscaler free cash flow fell from $264bn to $77bn on heavy capex; JPM's bull case requires 2027 capex $397bn above consensus. JPM recommends long 12-month vs short 3-month momentum, but warns this unwinds in 2Q27 as April's rally rolls off the 12-month lookback.
